'''Massoud Ali-Mohammadi''' ({{langx|fa|مسعود علی‌محمدی}}{{lrm}}; 24 August 1959 – 12 January 2010) was an Iranian [[Quantum field theory|quantum field theorist]] and [[Elementary particle physics|elementary-particle physicist]] and a [[distinguished professor]] of [[elementary particle physics]] at the [[University of Tehran]]'s Department of Physics.<ref>[http://physics.ut.ac.ir/~alimohmd/ Official Website of Professor Masoud Ali-Mohammadi at Department of Physics of University of Tehran] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100116031432/http://physics.ut.ac.ir/~alimohmd/ |date=16 January 2010}}.</ref> Ali-Mohammadi was the first [[PhD]] graduate student in physics of the [[Sharif University of Technology]]. He published some 53 articles and letters in peer-reviewed academic journals<ref>List of publications of Professor Masoud Alimohammadi as presented on the website of Department of Physics of University of Tehran: {{cite web |url=http://physics.ut.ac.ir/~alimohmd/publics.htm |title=University Of Tehran |access-date=12 January 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100115060705/http://physics.ut.ac.ir/~alimohmd/publics.htm |archive-date=15 January 2010}}.</ref> and wrote and translated several physics textbooks,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.adinehbook.com/gp/search?search-alias=books&author=%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%AF+%D8%B9%D9%84%DB%8C+%D9%85%D8%AD%D9%85%D8%AF%DB%8C&select-author=author-exact|title=مسعود علی محمدی - آدینه بوک|website=www.adinehbook.com}}</ref> including ''[[Modern Quantum Mechanics]]'', revised edition, by [[J. J. Sakurai]], which he translated from English into [[Persian language|Persian]] in collaboration with Hamidreza Moshfegh.

On 12 January 2010, Ali-Mohammadi was assassinated in front of his home in [[Tehran]], while leaving for university. [[Majid Jamali Fashi]] was convicted of his killing and executed on 15 May 2012.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-18068820 "Iran hangs 'Israel spy' over nuclear scientist killing"], BBC News, 15 May 2012.</ref> He stated that he had acted on the instructions of [[Mossad]] and had been trained in [[Tel Aviv]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Iran hangs 'Mossad agent' for scientist killing |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/iran-execution-majid-jamali-fashi-idINDEE84E09I20120515 |access-date=27 December 2021 |work=Reuters |date=15 May 2012 |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Ali-Mohammadi was born on 25 August 1959 (although some sources give 23 March 1961).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://english.khamenei.ir/news/8822/Iran-s-first-nuclear-martyr-A-look-at-the-life-of-Martyr-Massoud|title=Iran's first nuclear martyr: A look at the life of Martyr Massoud Ali-Mohammadi - Khamenei.ir}}</ref> He entered [[Shiraz University]] in 1978 where he obtained his BSc in 1985. He subsequently moved to the [[Sharif University of Technology]] in Tehran, to study for his MSc in physics. In 1988 he began with his PhD studies at this university as one of its first PhD students in physics. He obtained his PhD there in 1992.

==Research and achievements==
He was a [[Quantum field theory|quantum field theorist]] with interests in such diverse fields as [[condensed matter physics]] ([[quantum Hall effect]] in curved geometries), [[cosmology]] (modified gravity, [[dark energy]], etc.) and [[string theory]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://physics.ut.ac.ir/~alimohmd/publics.htm|title=List of publications |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100115060705/http://physics.ut.ac.ir/~alimohmd/publics.htm|archive-date=15 January 2010}}</ref> [[Quantum field theory]] is a subject matter quite distinct from [[nuclear physics]], [[nuclear engineering]] in general, and [[nuclear weapons]] and [[nuclear power]]. Iran's Atomic Energy Agency has in an official statement rejected media reports that Ali-Mohammadi was associated with [[Iran's nuclear program]].<ref>[http://tabnak.ir/fa/pages/?cid=81011 ''Alimohammadi was not employed by us'', in Persian, Tābnāk, 12 January 2010] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100114104538/http://www.tabnak.ir/fa/pages/?cid=81011 |date=14 January 2010 }}.</ref> However, in an interview published in the [[Christian Science Monitor]] in July 2014, his widow Mansoureh Karami spoke of his "top secret nuclear work".<ref name='CSM2014'>[https://www.csmonitor.com/World/Middle-East/2014/0717/Covert-war-against-Iran-s-nuclear-scientists-a-widow-remembers "Covert war against Iran's nuclear scientists: a widow remembers"], ''The Christian Science Monitor'', 17 July 2014. Retrieved 18 July 2014.</ref>

Ali-Mohammadi was a Council Member of [[International Centre for Synchrotron-Light for Experimental Science Applications in the Middle East]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sesame.org.jo/Council/CouncilMembers.aspx|title=The list of SESAME council members |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100221062640/http://www.sesame.org.jo/Council/CouncilMembers.aspx|archive-date=21 February 2010}}</ref> He was a professor at Tehran University's Physics faculty. Some sites claimed he was a professor at [[Imam Hossein University]].<ref name="dawn.com">{{Cite web|url=http://www.dawn.com/wps/wcm/connect/dawn-content-library/dawn/the-newspaper/front-page/top-iranian-nuclear-scientist-dies-in-bomb-attack-310|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604015759/http://www.dawn.com/wps/wcm/connect/dawn-content-library/dawn/the-newspaper/front-page/top-iranian-nuclear-scientist-dies-in-bomb-attack-310|url-status=dead|archive-date=4 June 2011|title=DAWN.COM}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=David M|url=http://threatswatch.org/analysis/2008/02/iaea-schweizer-kase/|title=Principal Analysis: IAEA Schweizer Käse|publisher=Threats Watch|date=29 February 2008|access-date=13 January 2012}}</ref> but Iranian analyst Muhammad Sahimi writes "He was not affiliated with the [[IRGC]]-controlled universities, namely Malek-e Ashtar and Emam Hossein universities."<ref name="SAHIMI" />

==Political views==
Ali Moghari, the director of the science department of Tehran University, described Ali-Mohammadi as an "apolitical professor", saying "he was a well-known professor but was not politically active."<ref name="nytimes">{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/01/13/world/middleeast/13iran.html|newspaper=The New York Times|title=Blast Kills Physics Professor in Tehran|first=Alan|last=Cowell|date=13 January 2010|access-date=12 May 2010}}</ref>

[[Ahmad Shirzad]] ([[Iranian Reformists|reformist]] member of the sixth [[Iranian Parliament]], professor of physics in Isfahan and close friend of Ali-Mohammadi) wrote: "In general his beliefs and actions were close to that of moderate Muslims. ... During the past couple of years he had ideologically become very close to the reformist movement. In the past few elections before the recent presidency election, he had voted for the reformist candidates and had been campaigning for them too." Shirzad adds that Ali-Mohammadi told him how he and his students took part in [[2009 Iranian election protests]], 16 June.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.gooya.com/politics/archives/2010/01/098981.php|title=(in Persian)|publisher=Gooya|access-date=13 January 2012}}</ref>

It was claimed by Tehran University's [[Basij]], or voluntary Islamist student militia, that his name was on a list of sanctioned individuals connected with Iranian nuclear program,<ref name="dawn.com" /> but he was not on a compiled list.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irantracker.org/us-policy/iran-policy-sanctioned-individuals-entities|title=Iran Policy: Sanctioned Individuals & Entities|publisher=IranTracker|date=21 July 2009|access-date=13 January 2012|url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120104220952/http://www.irantracker.org/us-policy/iran-policy-sanctioned-individuals-entities|archive-date=4 January 2012}}</ref> Ali-Mohammadi was among 240 university professors who signed a letter before the [[Iranian presidential election, 2009|2009 Presidential Election]] expressing support for the main opposition candidate, [[Mir Hossein Moussavi]].<ref name="nytimes" />

On reporting his burial, ''[[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al Jazeera]]'' reported on his lack of political involvement deepening the confusion over what motivation could have been behind the murder. They reported, "one of Ali Mohammadi's close friends (was quoted) as saying that the professor was never a political activist", and that, "... [Ali-]Mohammadi had very deep reformist tendencies but never mixed it up with his professional character." Ali Moghara, who heads the physics faculty at Tehran University, said Ali-Mohammadi was just a "world famous" physicist who engaged in "no political activity".<ref name="aljazeera">{{cite news|url=http://english.aljazeera.net/news/middleeast/2010/01/201011492553306143.html |title=Iranian bombing victim buried|publisher=Al Jazeera|access-date=13 January 2012}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Ali-Mohammadi was married to Mansoureh Karami ({{langx|fa|منصوره كرمی}}).<ref name=20120515iol>{{cite news|url=http://www.iol.co.za/news/world/iran-hangs-nuclear-scientist-killer-1.1296686|title=Iran hangs 'nuclear scientist' killer|date=15 May 2012|access-date=15 May 2012|newspaper=IOL News}}</ref>

==Assassination==
On 12 January 2010, at 07:58&nbsp;am, a motorbike rigged with explosives and parked near his car exploded while he was leaving home in [[Gheytarieh|Gheytariyeh]] neighbourhood of northern Tehran, for university.<ref name="nydailynews.com">{{cite news|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/news/world/2010/01/12/2010-01-12_iranian_nuclear_scientists_killed_in_bombing_tehran_blames_us_israel_for_attack.html|location=New York|newspaper=Daily News| title=Tehran nuclear scientist Massoud Ali-Mohammadi killed by bomb; Iran blames U.S., Israel for attack|date=12 January 2010}}</ref> The windows of residences around the scientist's home were shattered by the force of remote controlled explosion, and it was reported that two other people were also injured in the blast.<ref name="nydailynews.com" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://uk.biz.yahoo.com/12012010/323/photo/shattered-windows-near-massoud-ali-mohammadi-s-home.html |title=PHOTO: Shattered Windows Near Massoud Alimohammadi's home|access-date=13 January 2010}}{{dead link|date=May 2016|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://homylafayette.blogspot.com/2010/01/tehran-university-professor-massoud.html|title=Tehran University professor Massoud Alimohammadi assassinated: fact and fiction|publisher=Homy lafayette|date=12 January 2010|access-date=13 January 2012}}</ref>

Iranian state media accused Israel and the US of responsibility, while the [[US State Department]] called the allegation "absurd".<ref>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/8453401.stm Israel and US behind Tehran blast – Iranian state media], BBC, 13 January 2010</ref> [[Ynetnews]] stated that "there is no known connection between his participation" in the [[International Centre for Synchrotron-Light for Experimental Science Applications in the Middle East|SESAME]], an international [[Synchrotron radiation|synchrotron-radiation]] facility located in Jordan, and the assassination.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.ynetnews.com/articles/0,7340,L-3833674,00.html |title=Iranian physicist acquainted with Israeli scientists|newspaper=Ynetnews|date=20 June 1995|access-date=13 January 2012}}</ref> According to US intelligence sources, Israel is running a secret war against Iran, among techniques used are the killing of important persons in the Iranian atomic energy program.<ref name="Sherwell">{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/middleeast/israel/4640052/Israel-launches-covert-war-against-Iran.html|work=The Daily Telegraph|location=London|title=Israel launches covert war against Iran|first=Philip|last=Sherwell|date=16 February 2009|access-date=12 May 2010}}</ref>

Another source found the assassination of "a 50-year-old researcher with no prominent political voice, no published work with military relevance and no declared links to Iran's nuclear program", as puzzling, although there were comparisons with the disappearance of [[Shahram Amiri]] in 2009 and the death of [[Ardeshir Hosseinpour]] in 2007.<ref>[https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2010/01/12/iran-nuclear-physicist-ma_n_419676.html Iran Nuclear Physicist, Massoud Ali Mohammadi, Killed By Bomb] 12 January 2010</ref>

===Funeral===
On 14 January, Ali-Mohammadi was buried. His burial was arranged at Emamzādeh Ali-Akbar Chizar<ref>[http://www.ketabeavval.ir/tehran/2323.aspx Emamzādeh Ali-Akbar Chizar] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100519122627/http://www.ketabeavval.ir/tehran/2323.aspx |date=19 May 2010}}, in Persian, Ketāb-e Awwal.<br />- [[:fa:چیذر|Chizar]], Persian Wikipedia.</ref> in Tehran on Thursday 14 January 2010.<ref>[http://www.bornanews.com/vdci.uavct1apqbc2t.html The body of martyr Masoud Alimohammadi was laid to rest in Tehran's Ali-Akbar Shrine], in Persian, Bornā News Agency, Thursday, 14 January 2010.</ref><ref>[http://tabnak.ir/fa/pages/?cid=81242 Photographs: The funeral procession of Professor Masoud Alimohammadi] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100117070349/http://www.tabnak.ir/fa/pages/?cid=81242 |date=17 January 2010 }}, Tābnāk, Thursday, 14 January 2010.</ref>

Timesonline described it as "Supporters of Iran's regime hijacked the funeral." As his body was carried from his home in northern Tehran hundreds of government loyalists surrounded it and were shown on Iranian state television waving Iranian flags and chanting anti-American and anti-Israeli slogans.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110604145947/http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/news/world/middle_east/article6988037.ece Funeral of Iran scientist Masoud Ali-Mohammadi hijacked by regime loyalists], timesonline.co.uk. 15 January 2010.</ref>

===State investigation===
Twenty-four-year-old [[Majid Jamali Fashi]] was arrested days after the killing, and in January 2011, Iranian state television aired a confession by Fashi to having killed Ali-Mohammadi on behalf of [[Mossad]].{{citation needed|date=June 2019}} Fashi's arrest may have come as a result of a September 2009 [[WikiLeaks]] diplomatic cable from the US Embassy in [[Baku]], [[Azerbaijan]]. The cable quoted an Iranian source who was a licensed martial arts coach who was in contact with the Americans. Fashi was reportedly in Baku to participate in an international martial arts competition days before the cable was written.<ref>{{Cite web| last1=Ser | first1=Sam |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/wikileaks-report-may-have-doomed-iranian-mossad-agent/|title = Did a WikiLeaks document doom Iranian 'Mossad agent'?|website = [[The Times of Israel]] | date=16 May 2012 }}</ref> On 28 August 2011, Fashi was convicted and sentenced to death by the [[Islamic Revolutionary Court]].<ref name=vancouversun>{{cite news |url=https://vancouversun.com/technology/answers+murders+Iranian+nuclear+scientists/5332336/story.html|title=Few answers in murders of Iranian nuclear scientists|author=Jonathan Manthorpe|date=31 August 2011|work=The Vancouver Sun|location=Canada}}</ref> He was hanged on 15 May 2012 at [[Tehran]]'s [[Evin Prison]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/middle-east/iran-hangs-mossad-spy-majid-jamali-fashi-for-killing-scientist-7754332.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220512/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/middle-east/iran-hangs-mossad-spy-majid-jamali-fashi-for-killing-scientist-7754332.html |archive-date=12 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |work=The Independent |first=Donald |last=MacIntyre |title=Iran hangs 'Mossad spy' Majid Jamali Fashi for killing scientist |date=16 May 2012}}</ref>

===Media speculation===
The [[BBC]]'s Tehran correspondent [[Jon Leyne]] said "Iranian media were unusually quick off the mark to report the killing, to show television pictures, and to give the sort of details that usually only emerge after hours, days, or weeks in this secretive state".<ref>{{cite news| url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/8456076.stm|work=BBC News|title=Iran scientist killing: More questions than answers|date=13 January 2010|access-date=12 May 2010}}</ref> An anonymous former senior official expressed doubt about the official account of Ali-Mohammadi's assassination and expressed concern that the assassination could be used as an excuse for violence against opposition protesters: "This is an old trick. ... They did it themselves but blame it on opposition groups so that they can easily begin issuing death sentences for protesters. I think this means there could be more violence against the opposition."<ref name="nytimes" />

Opposition groups who monitor [[Hezbollah]], the militant Lebanese movement, in Tehran, claim that a member of Hezbollah, known by his pseudonym "Abu Nasser", was photographed at the scene of the explosion in Tehran's affluent [[Gheytarieh|Gheytarih]] suburb.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/news/world/middle_east/article6991081.ece| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604150412/http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/news/world/middle_east/article6991081.ece| url-status=dead| archive-date=4 June 2011|newspaper=The Times|location=London|title=Iranian dissident Masoud Ali Mohammadi killed by Arab hitman|first=Uzi|last=Mahnaimi|date=17 January 2010|access-date=12 May 2010}}</ref>

According to Iranian-Israeli analyst [[Meir Javedanfar]], It is "possible that [Ali-]Mohammadi was assassinated by a foreign intelligence agency" with the aim of stopping the [[Iranian nuclear program]] and also causing embarrassment for the government of Ahmadinejad.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2010/jan/12/iran-nuclear-scientist-mohammadi|newspaper=The Guardian|location=London|title=Is Iran losing the intelligence war?|date=12 January 2010|access-date=12 May 2010|first=Meir|last=Javedanfar}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Ungerleider|first=Neal|url=http://trueslant.com/nealungerleider/2010/01/12/who-killed-the-iranian-physicist/|title=Who killed the Iranian physicist?|publisher=True/Slant|date=19 January 2010|access-date=13 January 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120222192003/http://trueslant.com/nealungerleider/2010/01/12/who-killed-the-iranian-physicist/|archive-date=22 February 2012}}</ref> Flynt Leverett, director of [[New America Foundation]], said that while it is "highly unlikely that the United States was directly involved" in the assassination, it is "possible that a group or an individual" who received financial support as part of the $400 million US covert activities program initiated under Bush administration against Iran, might have carried out the assassination.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.raceforiran.com/flynt-leverett-on-world-focus-discusses-the-assassination-of-masoud-ali-mohammadi/comment-page-1#comment-2328|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130201024415/http://www.raceforiran.com/flynt-leverett-on-world-focus-discusses-the-assassination-of-masoud-ali-mohammadi/comment-page-1%23comment-2328|url-status=dead|title=Flynt Leverett on World Focus Discusses the Assassination of Masoud Ali Mohammadi|publisher=The Race for Iran|access-date=13 January 2012|archive-date=1 February 2013}}</ref>

However, Iranian analyst Muhammad Sahimi thinks it unlikely that the murder was directed against Iran's nuclear program as it is engineers, not nuclear physicists, who are "leading" that program, and in any case Ali-Mohammadi's research was in the general area of particle physics, "which is of a fundamental, rather than practical nature". Ali-Mohammadi was also not under contract with [[Atomic Energy Organization of Iran]], according to its spokesman [[Ali Shirzadian]], nor was he affiliated with the universities under the control of the [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|Revolutionary Guard]] ([[Malek-Ashtar University of Technology]] and [[Imam Hossein University]]).<ref name="SAHIMI">{{Cite web|url=http://www.pbs.org/wgbh/pages/frontline/tehranbureau/2010/01/who-murdered-prof-ali-mohammadi.html|title=Who murdered Prof. Ali-Mohammadi?|website=FRONTLINE - Tehran Bureau}}</ref> On the other hand, "a source in Tehran" told Sahimi that Ali-Mohammadi had worked with the [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|Islamic Revolution Guards]] "on several projects in the past," and this knowledge combined with the Guard's penchant for exacting vengeance against "anyone who deserts them and joins the opposition" adds to "the suspicion that the hardliners may have had something to do with" his murder.<ref name="SAHIMI"/>

''[[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al Jazeera]]'' reported that authorities on condition of anonymity have confirmed his involvement with Iranian nuclear program.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://english.aljazeera.net/news/middleeast/2010/01/201011273050938177.html|title=Bomb blast kills Iranian professor |publisher=Al Jazeera|access-date=13 January 2012}}</ref> ''[[The Economist]]'' also quoted anonymous Western sources describing him as "one of the most important people involved in the [nuclear] programme".<ref>{{cite news|title=Covert action against Iran: Who killed the professor?|url=http://www.economist.com/world/middleeast-africa/displaystory.cfm?story_id=15502383|newspaper=The Economist|date=11 February 2010|access-date=11 February 2010}}</ref> It was also reported that he was a professor at Tehran University's Physics faculty as well as a professor at the [[IRGC]] run, [[Imam Hossein University]] which houses a physics research center apparently under control of the IRGC.<ref name="dawn.com" /> There were also reports of a decapitation program as part of a covert war against Iran, with the aim of assassinating people that are or have been involved with Iranian nuclear program,<ref name="Sherwell" /> much like a similar successful program conducted in Iraq, resulting in assassination of hundreds of Iraqi scientists.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uruknet.info/?p=42278 |title=informazione dal medio oriente|publisher=uruknet|access-date=13 January 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://shr.aaas.org/emerging_issues/iraq.htm|title=Human Rights and Law|publisher=AAAS|access-date=13 January 2012}}</ref> There were also reports of Israel's involvement in these covert actions,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.studentnewsdaily.com/daily-news-article/israel-launches-covert-war-against-iran/|title=Israel Launches Covert War Against Iran|date=17 February 2009|publisher=Studentnewsdaily|access-date=13 January 2012}}</ref> while other reports suggested the creation of a joint assassination team put together by western democracies to neutralize Iranian scientists and engineers.<ref>{{cite web|last=Allam|first=Hannah|url=http://www.mcclatchydc.com/iran/story/80348.html|title=Iranian nuclear scientist goes missing in Saudi Arabia|publisher=McClatchyDC|access-date=13 January 2012|url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091214091400/http://www.mcclatchydc.com/iran/story/80348.html|archive-date=14 December 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://ahrcanum.wordpress.com/2010/01/12/dead-scientist-list-masoud-ali-mohammadi/|title=Dead Scientist List, Masoud Ali Mohammadi |publisher=Ahrcanum|date=16 January 2010|access-date=13 January 2012}}</ref>

An article in ''[[Time (magazine)|Time magazine]]'' claimed that a Western intelligence source confirmed the truth of the confession made by [[Majid Jamali Fashid]], who said he assassinated Massoud Ali-Mohammadi on behalf of [[Mossad]], Israel. The source confirmed that Iranian intelligence had cracked one cell trained and equipped by Mossad, and blamed a "third country" for exposing the cell.<ref name="time_mossad_cutting_back">{{cite news |url=https://world.time.com/2012/03/30/mossad-cutting-back-on-covert-operations-inside-iran-officials-say/ |title=Mossad Cutting Back on Covert Operations Inside Iran, Officials Say |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |date=30 March 2012 |access-date=12 April 2013 |author=Vick, Karl}}</ref><ref name=Haaretz_Mossad_scales_back>{{cite news|title=Report: Israel's Mossad scales back covert operations in Iran|url=https://www.haaretz.com/news/diplomacy-defense/report-israel-s-mossad-scales-back-covert-operations-in-iran-1.421776|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120331104636/http://www.haaretz.com/news/diplomacy-defense/report-israel-s-mossad-scales-back-covert-operations-in-iran-1.421776|url-status=dead|archive-date=31 March 2012|newspaper=Haaretz|access-date=1 April 2012|date=31 March 2012}}</ref>
